xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2359: reapMergedStrikeWorkspaces reaps FRESH strike workspaces (0 commits ahead of main looks 'merged')

plan.title: bug(deacon): reapMergedStrikeWorkspaces reaps FRESH strike workspaces (0 commits ahead of main looks 'merged')
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-4-8

narratives.Problem: reapMergedStrikeWorkspaces (src/lib/cloister/strike-workspace-reaper.ts:79) reaps a strike/<id> worktree when its branch is `ahead == 0` (git rev-list --count origin/main..branch). But a freshly-created strike branch — `git worktree add -b strike/<id> <ws> origin/main` in src/cli/commands/strike.ts:116 — sits at origin/main's HEAD with 0 authored commits, so it is also `ahead == 0` and indistinguishable from a merged branch by ancestry. Because runOne creates the worktree (strike.ts:180) BEFORE spawning the tmux session (strike.ts:187), a deacon patrol landing in that window sees `ahead == 0` and no live strike session, and reaps the worktree out from under the spawning agent — dumping it onto `main` (worktree-drift). Observed 2026-07-04: strike-pan-2357 reaped seconds after spawn, agent landed on main, refused to edit, escalated, produced nothing. The harm is not lost commits (there are none) but yanking an in-use worktree.
narratives.Proposal: Fix the reap predicate to require positive evidence the strike authored work that reached main, never merely `ahead == 0`. After the existing ahead check, add an authored-commits guard using `git rev-list --walk-reflogs --count <branch>`: skip (continue) when the count is <= 1. Empirically verified: a fresh branch has walk-reflogs count 1 (only 'branch: Created from origin/main'); a branch that authored a commit and ff-merged has count 2 while ahead stays 0 (the reflog is append-only and never shrinks on merge). So the reaper reaps only when `ahead == 0` AND `walk-reflogs count > 1`. Correct the module-header safety comment to describe the new invariant ('authored commits, all now in origin/main'). Extend the unit test exec mock to answer the new command and add regression tests. The guard errs safe: if the reflog is unavailable/expired the count reads 1 or the command errors (existing catch -> continue), so a merged branch would merely leak, never a fresh branch wrongly reaped.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No worktree-age grace window / timer (a band-aid on the spawn-race symptom; the reflog guard fixes the predicate at root cause).
- No change to strike spawn ordering (ensureStrikeWorktree before spawnAgent).
- No GitHub PR merged-state lookup (strikes ff-merge and open no PR, so PR state is not a usable signal).
- No fix for the narrow reused-stale-branch corner (a prior merged strike/<id> branch whose `git branch -D` was skipped, re-checked-out for a new strike during the spawn window) — pre-existing, out of scope, recorded as a hazard.
- Never touch feature/* worktrees or any non-strike branch.

autoDecisions.summary: Use `git rev-list --walk-reflogs --count <branch>` (authored-commits count) as the fresh-vs-merged discriminator.
autoDecisions.rationale: Ancestry (ahead==0) cannot distinguish a fresh branch from a ff-merged one; both have their tip contained in origin/main. The issue explicitly directs 'Guard on had-commits AND they are all in main'. The reflog count is exactly that signal and was empirically verified (fresh=1, merged=2 while ahead stays 0). Rejected GitHub PR-state (strikes open no PR) and a worktree-age grace window (a timer band-aid).

autoDecisions.summary: Keep the fix surgical: one predicate guard + module-header comment + regression tests, in one bead.
autoDecisions.rationale: The change is a genuinely indivisible unit — the tests prove the guard and the comment is the same diff. The spawn-race and reused-stale-branch corners are captured as hazards/NonGoals rather than expanded into scope, per surgical-change discipline.

items.title: Guard strike reap on authored commits (walk-reflogs > 1), not just ahead==0

expected_outputs: strike-workspace-reaper.test.ts passes including the new fresh-branch regression tests

narrative.Action: In src/lib/cloister/strike-workspace-reaper.ts, inside reapMergedStrikeWorkspaces, AFTER the existing `if (ahead !== '0') continue;` check (line ~79), add an authored-commits guard. Run `git rev-list --walk-reflogs --count <branch>` (quote the branch with JSON.stringify, cwd: projectRoot, encoding: 'utf-8'); on error `continue` (leave for a future patrol). Parse the trimmed stdout as a number; if it is <= 1 `continue` (a never-committed branch — fresh strike, e.g. worktree add -b strike/<id> ... origin/main sits at main with a single 'Created from origin/main' reflog entry). Only when the count > 1 proceed to the existing `git worktree remove` + `git branch -D` reap. Update the module-header block comment (lines ~1-16) so the safety invariant reads that a worktree is reaped only when its branch AUTHORED commits that are now all in origin/main (walk-reflogs > 1 AND ahead == 0) and no live strike session exists — replacing the current '0 commits ahead — nothing unmerged is ever lost' wording which conflates fresh with merged. In src/lib/cloister/__tests__/strike-workspace-reaper.test.ts, extend wireExec to answer the new command: match `cmd.includes('--walk-reflogs --count')` BEFORE the existing `cmd.includes('rev-list --count')` branch (the new command also contains 'rev-list' but not the contiguous 'rev-list --count'); return a per-branch reflog count from a new `reflogByBranch` param defaulting to '2' (merged-like) so existing tests keep reaping. Add regression tests per the acceptance criteria.

items.title: Given a strike branch with ahead==0 and walk-reflogs count '1' (fresh, never committed) and no live session, reapMergedStrikeWorkspaces does NOT run `git worktree remove` for it and returns no action for that worktree.

Given a strike branch with ahead==0 and walk-reflogs count '2' (authored+merged) and no live session, reapMergedStrikeWorkspaces still runs `git worktree remove` AND `git branch -D` for it (PAN-1882 cleanup preserved).
Given the `git rev-list --walk-reflogs --count` command throws for a branch, reapMergedStrikeWorkspaces skips that worktree (does not run `git worktree remove`) and continues to other worktrees.

The module-header comment in strike-workspace-reaper.ts states the reap condition as authored commits now all in origin/main (walk-reflogs > 1 AND ahead == 0), not '0 commits ahead'; npm run typecheck completes without errors.
